registry_scope: Steel's definition (voluntary delay of an intended action despite expecting to be worse off for it); the emotion-regulation account (Sirois and Pychyl); temporal motivation theory and the intention-action gap; akrasia as the classical ancestor; self-forgiveness and self-compassion as evidence-backed repairs; the practice family (implementation intentions, temptation bundling, precommitment). Nearby terms: akrasia, delay, intention-action gap, temporal discounting. Question draft: Why does a person who knows better still postpone, and what actually closes the gap between intending and doing?

synthesis: Handoff synthesis for the next writer (T+41): the 26 read cards support a five-movement dossier: (1) The definition - Steel's voluntary-delay-despite-expecting-to-be-worse-off, with the akrasia ancestry (Socrates denies it, Aristotle documents it in NE VII; SEP Weakness of Will is the carrier for the debate); (2) The mechanism - not laziness but short-term mood repair: Sirois and Pychyl's give-in-to-feel-good (MO045, the White Rose PDF is openable and load-bearing), with TMT (MO005, Steel et al. 2018 N=7,400) as the timing model and the pigeon delay-reduction study as the boundary; (3) The person-level moderators - impulsiveness, task aversiveness, self-efficacy (Steel 2007 meta-analysis, PubMed 17201571), with the honest mixed sleep/depletion record (MO051); (4) The repairs - self-forgiveness (Wohl, Pychyl and Bennett 2010), self-compassion (MO050), if-then plans (K153, Sheeran's r+ = 0.53 intention-behavior gap), temptation bundling (MO029 with Kirgios 2020), fresh starts (MO028), environment (MO049), and the Seneca timing counsel (Pre-commitment as wisdom: every emotion at the start is weak); (5) The narrative side - temporal self-appraisal (failures get pushed back in time) and the reform-capable reading of akrasia (A057, NE VII.8).
